business_problem: Repsol needed to anticipate service-station store demand, reduce stock-outs and waste, and cut manual delivery-note entry so station teams could spend more time on customer service.
solution_summary: Repsol built two AI-driven workflows for service-station store operations. The internal Suggested ordering application uses predictive AI and optimization algorithms to estimate replenishment needs for roughly 1,000 items per station and generate order recommendations two or three times a week. About 900 forecasting models and another 900 optimization models run daily, and the system improves as it absorbs new data and learns from decisions made at each station. Recommendations are delivered to station managers, who can accept or adjust them using local context. In parallel, Repsol is piloting Automatic delivery note reading: employees photograph supplier delivery notes on a mobile phone, generative AI extracts fields such as date, supplier, items, and quantities, and the structured output is uploaded into Repsol's system for operator validation. Together, the workflows combine AI automation with human oversight to improve availability and reduce repetitive administrative work.

solution_components.name: Suggested ordering
solution_components.role: Uses predictive AI and optimization algorithms to calculate replenishment needs and recommend what items each station should restock and in what quantity.

solution_components.name: Automatic delivery note reading
solution_components.role: Uses generative AI to read photographed delivery notes and extract structured fields for upload into Repsol's system.

data_flow: Operational station data feeds daily forecasting and optimization models that produce replenishment suggestions for managers, who accept or adjust the recommendations before orders are placed. For delivery notes, an employee photographs the document on a mobile phone, generative AI extracts date, supplier, items, and quantities, and the validated structured output is uploaded into Repsol's system.
integration_points: Mobile phones used by station employees
Repsol's internal system for registering delivery-note information
business_outcome: Repsol reports higher product availability, fewer stock-outs, orders better aligned with demand, less manual data entry, fewer transcription errors, and more employee time for higher-value customer tasks, while retaining human judgment in operational decisions.

architecture_clues: Suggested ordering is deployed at scale across hundreds of stations, while automatic delivery note reading remains in the testing phase at some stations.
Human validation is built into both workflows: managers can adjust replenishment recommendations, and operators review extracted delivery-note results.
The delivery-note workflow uses mobile-photo capture as the document ingestion method.
